# Integration Requirements Checklist: OpenCode Host Support

**Purpose**: Validate the completeness, clarity, and consistency of the OpenCode integration
requirements (spec + plan) before implementation — focused on the external-dependency, safety,
and idempotency aspects unique to adding a third traced host.
**Created**: 2026-09-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements. Focus areas selected autonomously (YOLO mode, no interview): external
integration reliability, safety/non-blocking contract, and idempotent ingestion — the three
highest-risk dimensions of adding a new, externally-triggered host to this tracer. Depth:
Standard. Audience: Reviewer (PR).
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.
Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is
satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for what happens when the OpenCode plugin cannot reach the
  tracer's endpoint at all (daemon not running)? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the behavior specified for an OpenCode event type not in the plan's mapped set
  (R2) — e.g. a future OpenCode version adding a new lifecycle event? [Completeness, Spec FR-009]
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for setup behavior when OpenCode is detected but the global
  plugin directory is not writable (permissions)? [Gap, Spec FR-006]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for what a developer sees if the OpenCode plugin is
  installed but never actually invoked (e.g. OpenCode never used after setup)? [Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is "a few seconds" (SC-001, dashboard update latency) quantified precisely enough to
  be objectively tested, or does it need an explicit upper bound? [Clarity, Spec SC-001]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "additive" (FR-007, never overwriting existing OpenCode plugins) precise enough to
  distinguish "installing a new file" from "modifying a shared config", given OpenCode's plugin
  directories can hold multiple independent files? [Clarity, Spec FR-007]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the idempotency key — `(session_id, message_id)` for turns, `(message_id,
  tool_call_id)` for tool calls — stated precisely enough to be independently verifiable by a
  reviewer without reading the implementation? [Clarity, Spec Clarifications]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Are the tool-call classification rules (FR-003, research R6) consistent with the
  existing `ToolCall['type']` vocabulary used for Copilot CLI and Claude Code, with no OpenCode
  case left ambiguous between two categories (e.g. custom plugin-defined tools)? [Consistency,
  Spec FR-003]
- [ ] CHK009 Do the safety-contract requirements for `/opencode/hook` (plan Technical Context,
  contracts/opencode-hook.md) match the existing `/claude/hook` contract exactly, with no
  unexplained divergence in status codes or error handling? [Consistency]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK010 Can SC-002 ("100% of tool calls... correctly classified... rather than 'unknown'")
  be objectively verified given that `unknown` is not a value in the existing `ToolCall['type']`
  enum — is the failure mode this criterion guards against clearly defined? [Measurability, Spec
  SC-002]
- [ ] CHK011 Can SC-003 ("zero discrepancy" between reported and provider usage) be verified when
  a model has no pricing entry, given FR-004 explicitly allows a zero-cost fallback in that case?
  [Consistency, Spec SC-003 vs FR-004]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK012 Are requirements defined for an OpenCode session that produces tool calls but no
  assistant message (e.g. an aborted turn)? [Coverage, Edge Case, Gap]
- [x] CHK013 Are requirements defined for concurrent OpenCode sessions in the same project
  directory (two terminals, same repo)? [Coverage, Gap]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Is the fallback/ungrouped project behavior for a non-git OpenCode session (FR-010)
  specified precisely enough to know whether it is a single shared fallback project or one per
  working directory? [Clarity, Spec FR-010]
- [x] CHK015 Is the expected end state defined for a turn that never receives a terminal
  `session.idle`/`session.error` signal (process killed) — e.g. does it remain `running`
  indefinitely, or is there a bounded timeout? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK016 Are performance/latency expectations for the hook receiver itself (not just the
  dashboard update) quantified, given the safety contract requires it never delay the developer's
  OpenCode session? [Clarity, Plan Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for what the tracer logs (and does not log) when an OpenCode
  payload is malformed, consistent with the constitution's prohibition on logging raw prompt
  content by default? [Gap, Constitution Additional Constraints]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK018 Is the assumption that OpenCode's plugin `message.updated` event reliably includes
  per-message token usage validated, or is it flagged as an open risk with a documented fallback?
  [Assumption, Research R2/R9 Outstanding Items]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the dependency on `@opencode-ai/plugin`'s type definitions (for exact event field
  names) documented as a planning-time risk rather than an implicit assumption baked silently into
  the design? [Dependency, Research R2]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer
  evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify`
  and `/speckit-clarify` and is not affected by this file.
